paper_metadata.title: Development of low-density γ/γ′ Co-Al-Ta-based superalloys with high solvus temperature

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The present paper reports the development of W -, Mo-, and V -free and Ni - and Cr-containing Co-Al-Ta-based superalloys.

evidence.section: 4. Summary
evidence.quote: The present study reports the alloy development of the γ/γ′ Co -Al-Ta-based superalloys, which are W-, Mo -, and V -free.

evidence.section: 4. Summary
evidence.quote: The γ′ phase stability and γ/γ′ composition range were raised by increasing the Ni content in Co-Ni-Al-Ta quaternary alloys under study.

evidence.section: 4. Summary
evidence.quote: The Co-30Ni-12Al-4Ta-xCr (x = 0, 4, 8, and 12) alloys were prepared, which solvus temperature values changed slightly and densities with the Cr content.

evidence.section: 4. Summary
evidence.quote: The developed Co-30Ni-12Al-4Ta-12Cr alloy exhibits a very good combination of high solvus temperature (~1152 °C), low density (~8.38 g/cm 3), low γ/γ′ lattice misfit (~+0.33%), and low coarsening rate of γ′ precipitate (~1.95 × 10 -27 m/s at 900 °C ).

evidence.section: 2.1 Sample preparation
evidence.quote: Small button ingots (~30 g) were arc-melted (under a high-purity Ar atmosphere) using raw materials of Co, Al, Ta, Ni, and Cr (a purity of at least 99.9 wt.%).

evidence.section: 2.1 Sample preparation
evidence.quote: A solution treatment at 1300 °C for 24 h was performed for all samples before annealing at lower temperatures.

evidence.section: 3.3.5 Solvus temperature and density comparison
evidence.quote: The solvus temperature of 12Cr alloy (~1152 °C) is higher than that of W -containing Co-9Al-9W (1000 °C) and Co-9Al-10W-2Ta (1098 °C) [10] alloys, and also exceeds those of Cr-containing Co-Ta-V-based (~965 °C) [30], Co-Al-Mo-Ta-based (1038-1105 °C) [24, 25], and Co-11Ti-15Cr (1100 °C) alloys [34].

evidence.section: 3.3.5 Solvus temperature and density comparison
evidence.quote: Meanwhile, the studied 12Cr alloy exhibits very low mass density (~8.38 g/cm3), as compared to those of W -containing Co-Al-W-based [ 20, 74] and commercially available conventional cobalt-based Mar-M-302 (Co-21.5Cr-10W-9Ta-0.85C-0.2Zr-0.005B, wt.%) superalloys [56], which amount to 9.54-10.1 and 9.2 g/cm3, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.3.6 Mechanical properties
evidence.quote: For the studied 12Cr alloy, t he yield strength value drops from ~690 MPa at ambient temperature to ~640 MPa at 600 °C, and then rises to ~770 MPa at 700 °C, followed by a rapid drop to ~460 MPa at 900 °C.
